skill.name: nansen-holder-analysis
skill.description: Evaluate whether a token is held by smart money wallets or retail-heavy flow using Nansen holder, flow, and buyer-seller data.
skill.summary: Evaluate token holder quality with Nansen smart money, flow intelligence, and buyer-seller label data.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally runs the Nansen CLI and requires a NANSEN_API_KEY for data access. I found no prompt injection text or unrelated exfiltration instructions, but the external command and secret exposure risks are real for a community skill.

remediation.issue: NANSEN_API_KEY is required by the skill.
remediation.suggestion: Document that the key is used only by the Nansen CLI, recommend a least-privilege key, and tell users never to paste the key into prompts.

remediation.issue: The skill executes external Nansen CLI commands.
remediation.suggestion: Keep Bash permissions restricted to nansen commands and validate or quote token and chain inputs before command construction.

content.value_statement: Token teams need to know whether holders are high-quality wallets or short-term retail flow. This skill uses Nansen CLI commands to compare smart money holders, label flows, and buyer quality.
actual_capabilities: Runs Nansen holder analysis with smart money filtering and a top holder limit.
Reviews holder labels, value in USD, ownership share, and balance changes.
Compares token flow by labels such as smart trader, whale, exchange, and fresh wallets.
Checks recent buyers and sellers by wallet label and trading volume.
Highlights red flags and green flags for holder quality.
limitations: Requires a valid NANSEN_API_KEY and the nansen CLI package.
Nansen data coverage and rate limits affect results.
The holder endpoint does not support native or wrapped tokens.
The example defaults to Ethereum and needs a specific token contract address.

use_cases.title: Screen a New Token
use_cases.description: Check whether a newly listed token has credible smart money ownership before deeper due diligence.

use_cases.title: Monitor Portfolio Holder Quality
use_cases.description: Track holder quality changes for portfolio tokens using smart money balances and label flows.

use_cases.title: Review Holder Risk Signals
use_cases.description: Identify retail-heavy or fresh-wallet-dominated holder bases before communications or risk review.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Holder Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a simple smart money holder review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze holder quality for [token contract] on [chain]. Use the Nansen holder-analysis skill and explain whether smart money ownership is meaningful.

prompt_templates.title: Label Flow Comparison
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare key wallet label flows for a token.
prompt_templates.prompt: For [token contract] on [chain], compare smart trader, whale, exchange, and fresh wallet flows. Summarize red flags and green flags.

prompt_templates.title: Buyer and Seller Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Assess whether recent buyers look higher quality than sellers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review recent buyers and sellers for [token contract] on [chain]. Separate accumulation, distribution, and neutral activity by wallet label.

prompt_templates.title: Holder Quality Memo
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a fuller research note from all available Nansen views.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a holder quality memo for [token contract] on [chain]. Combine smart money holders, balance changes, label flows, and buyer-seller quality.

output_examples.input: Analyze holder quality for an Ethereum token.
output_examples.output: The token shows moderate smart money ownership, but recent flow is dominated by fresh wallets. Treat momentum as fragile until label quality improves.

output_examples.input: Compare buyers and sellers over the latest Nansen window.
output_examples.output: Smart trader labels are small net buyers while exchange labels show distribution. The result suggests selective accumulation with liquidity pressure.

output_examples.input: Check whether top holders support a quality thesis.
output_examples.output: Top holders include fund and smart trader labels with stable seven-day balances. This supports a stronger holder quality signal.

best_practices: Use a specific token contract address and confirm the chain before analysis.
Compare smart money holder data with label flow and buyer-seller activity.
Treat fresh wallet inflows as a warning signal until stronger labels confirm quality.
anti_patterns: Using native or wrapped token symbols when a contract address is required.
Making a buy or sell decision from one holder snapshot alone.
Pasting private API keys into prompts or command text.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It analyzes token holder labels, smart money ownership, label-based flows, and recent buyer-seller quality using Nansen data.

faq.question: Does it require a Nansen account?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires the nansen CLI and a valid NANSEN_API_KEY in the environment.

faq.question: Can it analyze native or wrapped tokens?
faq.answer: No. The holder endpoint does not support native or wrapped tokens, so use a specific token contract address.

faq.question: Which chains can it analyze?
faq.answer: It can analyze chains supported by the installed Nansen CLI. The included example uses Ethereum.

faq.question: Does it provide trading advice?
faq.answer: No. It provides holder quality research signals that should be combined with broader due diligence.

faq.question: Will it expose my API key?
faq.answer: The skill expects the key in the environment for the Nansen CLI. Do not paste private keys or API keys into prompts.
